study: A decoded reach driven through a simulated human arm, and controllers rejected on a macaque arm model
what: Two decoded components of fingertip velocity from a macaque reaching session were turned into shoulder and elbow goals for a simulated human arm with 63 muscles; separately, controllers for a macaque arm model were scored on recorded cases set aside for them.

why_some_numbers_have_no_macro: Whole numbers below 100, and round numbers that double as percentages or durations elsewhere in the papers, have no macro: the build would otherwise refuse the same digits wherever another section types them as an ordinary number. The papers print them as words or as plain digits; each is listed here with its source so that it can be checked.
limits: Simulation only. The step from a macaque's fingertip velocity to a human shoulder and elbow is an engineering rule, not a measured correspondence.
The corrected arm follows its own command closely partly because the correction may change the command; the comparison against one common reference is the fairer one.
Three controllers for the macaque arm model were rejected on recorded cases; the planning controller had done better than the constant command on made-up movements first.
The reference muscle lengths come from tracking and a body model, not from measured muscle fibres.
